text:
Whoever gives a heart to this minute,

stiff and frozen, to this flowing without harmony,

to this painful and cold blood of mine,

to this dry grief without voice or mourning;


whoever polishes edges on the rough diamond,

whoever returns to the bird its lost guide,

whoever makes solitude and company,

voice and silence for the absolute song;


whoever gives me back all my landscapes

and sees, gathered in my stillness,

the longed-for coast and veil of my journeys;


whoever turns health back to me with her wound,

whoever dresses my dreams in her garments,

formless longing! will fulfill my life.

translation.title: Deserted Love
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem as an invocation to the one who can restore landscape, guide, wound, and life.
